summary: First-order equation. 1 method applies: Integrating factor (linear).

methods.name: Separation of variables
methods.reason: The right-hand side \(x - 2 y\) cannot be written as a product \(g(x)\,h(y)\), so the variables cannot be separated.

methods.name: Integrating factor (linear)
methods.reason: It can be written as \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\) with \(p = 2\) and \(q = x\).

steps.title: Solve for the derivative
steps.text: Rearrange the equation so the derivative is alone on the left.

steps.title: Write in standard form
steps.text: Move the \(y\) term to the left so the equation reads \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\).

steps.title: Find the integrating factor
steps.text: The integrating factor is \(\mu = e^{\int p\,dx}\).

steps.title: Multiply through by the integrating factor
steps.text: After multiplying by \(\mu\), the left side is exactly the derivative of the product \(\mu\,y\) (product rule in reverse).
latex: e^{2 x}\,\frac{dy}{dx} + 2 e^{2 x}\,y = x e^{2 x}

steps.title: Integrate both sides
steps.text: Integrate with respect to \(x\). The left side undoes the derivative.
latex: e^{2 x}\,y = \frac{\left(2 x - 1\right) e^{2 x}}{4} + C

substeps.title: Right integral
latex: \int x e^{2 x}\,dx = \frac{\left(2 x - 1\right) e^{2 x}}{4}

steps.title: Solve for y
steps.text: Divide both sides by the integrating factor.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked symbolically by substituting back into the equation.

methods.verify_note: Checked symbolically by substituting back into the equation.

methods.name: Exact equation
methods.reason: Written as \(M\,dx + N\,dy = 0\), exactness needs \(\partial M/\partial y = \partial N/\partial x\). Here they are \(2\) and \(0\), and the simpler methods above already apply.

methods.name: Bernoulli substitution
methods.reason: The equation does not have the form \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\,y^n\) with \(n \ne 0, 1\).

methods.name: Homogeneous substitution (y = vx)
methods.reason: The right-hand side cannot be written as a function of \(y/x\) alone.

methods.name: Laplace transform
methods.reason: It needs initial conditions at \(x = 0\); add them to see this method.
